solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Pet at the chemist’s, the old story (4,2,5)

blocks.note: puss = a pet cat
Boots is the big British chain of chemist's shops, so 'at the chemist's' = IN BOOTS

annotation.surface: Someone spots a cat wandering around a pharmacy and recognises a familiar tale.
annotation.walkthrough: Boots is Britain's best-known high-street chemist, which is the whole trick: a cat at the chemist's is literally a puss in Boots.
annotation.definitionFit: Puss in Boots is an old fairy tale about a clever cat.

entries.clue: Pound and a penny: let’s start to eat out (6)

annotation.definitionNote: the clue gives the verb (what the tool does); the answer is the tool that pounds

indicatorNotes.start to: the start of 'eat' is its first letter
indicatorNotes.out: 'out' as in wild or disordered: the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: p = penny
anagram fodder
first letter of eat, added to the fodder
anagram indicator: LETS + E are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone counting coins announces it is time to go out for a meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money next to 'a penny', but it is the verb: a pestle is what you pound with in a mortar.
annotation.definitionFit: A pestle is the club-shaped tool used to pound things in a mortar.

entries.clue: In great misery, God’s help found so transforming (6,2,7)

indicatorNotes.transforming: the letters are transformed into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A believer in deep despair finds that divine help changed everything.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a conversion story, which suits an answer taken from Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, where Christian sinks into the Slough of Despond.
annotation.definitionFit: The Slough of Despond, a bog in The Pilgrim's Progress, is proverbial for a state of deep despair.

entries.clue: Better holding is made up (10)

indicatorNotes.holding: the outer word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: bettered = improved
used as it stands, placed inside IMPROV…ED

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a better-looking plot of land has been invented.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' has to be read as a past tense, bettered, to give IMPROVED; 'made up' means invented on the spot, not reconciled.
annotation.definitionFit: Improvised means made up on the spot, without preparation.

entries.clue: Bowled, do you agree? Not if these result (4)

annotation.definitionNote: an allusive definition: the runs that come about when the ball beats the bat but not the stumps

blocks.note: b = bowled on a cricket scorecard
the answer to 'do you agree?'

annotation.surface: A cricketer asks whether everyone agrees he was bowled, only to be told otherwise.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket, byes are runs scored when the ball passes the batter and the wicketkeeper without touching anything; if the ball had hit the stumps the batter would be bowled, so no byes.
annotation.definitionFit: Byes are runs taken when the bowled ball misses bat and stumps alike, the opposite of being bowled.

entries.clue: Compose in too ornate a style, but finished properly, we hear (9)

annotation.definition: Compose in too ornate a style

indicatorNotes.we hear: the second part is what we hear, not what is written

blocks.note: the game is over = finished
right = properly, said the same as WRITE

annotation.surface: A writer is told the prose is too flowery, though at least it was completed correctly.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pretends to be a critic's verdict, which is why the definition and the wordplay both sound like comments on the same piece of writing.
annotation.definitionFit: To overwrite is to write in an overly elaborate, ornate style.

entries.clue: Not the usual way to classify (7)

blocks.note: St = street, a way
to range = to arrange in ranks or classes

annotation.surface: Someone objects to an unconventional method of sorting things.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, 'the usual way to classify', so the split after 'usual' is hard to see; 'way' is a street, abbreviated ST.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym phrased as a negative: whatever departs from the usual is odd or unfamiliar.

entries.clue: He directed men and boys to conserve energy source first (5,6)

indicatorNotes.to conserve: SONS keeps the other letters inside it
indicatorNotes.first: the source comes first, then the energy

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, ordinary soldiers
boys = sons; this is the outer word
a well is a source of water
E = energy, after WELL because the source comes first

annotation.surface: A plea to men and boys to save power by using the main supply first.
annotation.walkthrough: OR for 'men' is a crossword staple: other ranks. 'Source first' fixes the order, WELL then E, before SONS closes around the pair.
annotation.definitionFit: Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane, among other films.

entries.clue: Don’t hold back Lady Macbeth’s feeling about her spot? (3,4,2)

annotation.definition2: Lady Macbeth’s feeling about her spot?

blocks.note: the plain meaning: say it, speak up

blocks.clueFragment: Lady Macbeth’s feeling about her spot?
blocks.note: she cries 'Out, damned spot!', so she wants it out

annotation.surface: A confidant urges Lady Macbeth to confess what she really feels about that bloodstain.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half leans on the sleepwalking scene in Macbeth, where Lady Macbeth scrubs at imagined blood crying 'Out, damned spot!'; the question mark flags the whimsy.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Out with it!' urges someone to stop holding back and say what they mean.

entries.clue: Big band music be hanged (5)

blocks.note: the jazz style of the big bands
the fate of a man on the gallows, left dangling

annotation.surface: Someone bursts out with a grumpy dismissal of big band music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Be hanged' reads as a curse on the music, but it is the second definition: to swing for a crime is to be hanged for it.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is the jazz of Goodman and Basie in the 1930s and 40s; the other is old slang for dangling from the gallows, as in 'he'll swing for it'.

entries.clue: Most precise projectile fired into sniper’s lair (9)

indicatorNotes.fired into: one piece is shot into the middle of the other

blocks.note: a sniper's nest; this is the outer word
an arrow is a projectile, placed inside N…EST

annotation.surface: A marksman's shot, aimed with great accuracy, lands in an enemy sniper's hide.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all shooting, so 'Most precise' reads as praise for the shot rather than the definition, as in the narrowest of margins.
annotation.definitionFit: Narrowest can mean most exact or strict, as in the narrowest interpretation.

entries.clue: Dangerous activity for the most gentlemanly competitor (7,5)

blocks.note: bungee jumping, BASE jumping and the like
a good sport plays fair; the most extreme one is the most gentlemanly

annotation.surface: A risky pastime is suggested as fit only for the most courteous of rivals.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half reads 'sport' as a person, as in 'be a sport', and 'extreme' as the superlative.
annotation.definitionFit: An extreme sport is a high-risk activity such as skydiving or free climbing.

entries.clue: Brochure made from the tiniest bit of tree? (7)

blocks.note: a printed handout
botanically, one small division of a compound leaf

annotation.surface: Someone muses on how little of a tree goes into making a pamphlet.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests paper made from wood pulp; the second sense is botanical, a leaflet being a little leaf, and the question mark flags the stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a small printed sheet or brochure handed out to people.

entries.clue: Oozing round one side of lid, about to drop off (6)

indicatorNotes.round: the outer word goes round the other
indicatorNotes.one side of: one edge of 'lid', its first letter

blocks.note: seepy = oozing; this is the outer word
first letter of lid, placed inside S…EEPY

annotation.surface: Something sticky is seeping round the edge of a lid that is about to fall off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drop off' pretends to be about the lid falling; in the definition it means nodding off to sleep.
annotation.definitionFit: Sleepy describes someone about to drop off to sleep.

entries.clue: Brandish gun, a fine specimen (9)

blocks.note: to brandish something is to show it off
piece = a gun, in slang

annotation.surface: Someone waves a firearm about, admiring it as a beautiful example of its kind.
annotation.walkthrough: PIECE for gun is American gangster slang; the surface keeps the weapon in view so 'fine specimen' reads as praise for it.
annotation.definitionFit: A showpiece is an outstanding example, one fit to be put on display.

entries.clue: In brief ceremony almost nothing about one could be more richly stylish (7)

indicatorNotes.brief: cut short: the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.almost: not quite all of the word

blocks.note: RITE without its last letter
ZERO without its last letter; the outer piece
I = one, placed inside Z…ER

annotation.surface: A pared-down ceremony, with next to nothing spent on anyone, might turn out more elegant.
annotation.walkthrough: RITZY comes from the Ritz hotels, a byword for luxury; two different words for 'shortened' do the trimming here.
annotation.definitionFit: Ritzy means luxuriously smart, so ritzier is more richly stylish.

entries.clue: Plague is to lessen after time (5)

indicatorNotes.after: the lessening comes after the time

blocks.note: t = time
to ease pain is to lessen it

annotation.surface: A statement that an epidemic fades as time passes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plague' looks like the disease, a noun; here it is the verb, to pester someone.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Plague' in its verb sense, to pester persistently, is what a tormenting sibling does with jibes.

entries.clue: Diver circles a good lake (6)

indicatorNotes.circles: the diver goes round the other letters

blocks.note: a loon is a diving bird; this is the outer word
used as it stands
g = good, placed with A inside L…OON

annotation.surface: A scuba diver swims in circles around a pleasant lake.
annotation.walkthrough: The diver is a bird: the loon, called a diver in Britain, which is why it circles rather than dives.
annotation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of shallow water cut off from the sea, a kind of lake.

entries.clue: Chief bird showing off (8)

blocks.note: a swan is a bird
a king is a chief

annotation.surface: The dominant bird in a flock struts about displaying itself.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces go in the other order from the clue: bird first, then chief, as in 'the swan king'. To swank is British for to show off.
annotation.definitionFit: Swanking is British slang for showing off or swaggering.

entries.clue: Cover where some dogs like to sprawl (7)

annotation.definition2: where some dogs like to sprawl

blocks.note: to extend across part of something, as roof tiles do

blocks.clueFragment: where some dogs like to sprawl
blocks.note: a lapdog likes to lie over a lap

annotation.surface: A dog blanket placed where pets like to stretch out.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as OVER LAP, where small dogs love to drape themselves.
annotation.definitionFit: To overlap something is to extend over and partly cover it.

entries.clue: Observe diluted gallon coming to the boil (8)

blocks.note: to observe is to see
diluted = thinned, thin
g = gallon

annotation.surface: Someone watches a watered-down gallon of liquid heat up on the stove.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diluted gallon' reads as one thing, but it splits into THIN and the abbreviation G.
annotation.definitionFit: Seething describes liquid bubbling as it comes to the boil, and by extension a person fuming.

entries.clue: Don’t delay rushed, curt thank-you note? (2,4,4,3,7)

blocks.note: the proverb urging you to act now
read as a telegram: a clipped apology for haste, then thanks for the gift

annotation.surface: Someone dashing off a terse note of thanks, with no time to linger.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the second half as a telegram: 'No time. Like the present.' It is short because the writer is rushed, and it thanks the giver for a present.
annotation.definitionFit: 'There's no time like the present' is the saying that tells you not to put things off.

entries.clue: Gang regularly taken in school run a pain (7)

indicatorNotes.taken in: one piece is taken inside the others

blocks.note: a school of whales is also a pod
second and fourth letters of gAnG, placed after POD
r = run, in cricket scoring
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A gang is regularly picked up during the school run, and it is a nuisance.
annotation.walkthrough: The school run, driving children to school, is the obvious reading, but 'school' here is a group of whales and 'a pain' holds the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Podagra is gout, especially in the big toe, a painful condition.

entries.clue: Unbalanced, I am helped to avoid area (3-5)

indicatorNotes.to avoid: the area is left out of the word

blocks.note: 'I am' is formally 'one is', contracted to ONE'S
helped = aided
a = area; taken out of AIDED to leave IDED

annotation.surface: Someone admits to being lopsided, having been helped to steer clear of a place.
annotation.walkthrough: The formal pronoun 'one' stands for 'I', so 'I am' becomes 'one is', written ONE'S.
annotation.definitionFit: Used of a contest or argument, both describe something tilted heavily in one direction.

entries.clue: Wrongly suggesting eastern and southern area of US? (7)

annotation.definition: Wrongly suggesting eastern and southern area of US?

blocks.note: read the answer as 'middle of WEST': the middle letters of WEST are E and S, eastern and southern
the real meaning: a region of the United States, nowhere near the east or south

annotation.surface: A remark that a US region's name gives a misleading idea of where it is.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as MID WEST and it describes the middle of the word WEST, which is E and S; the region itself is in the north-central United States.
annotation.definitionFit: The Midwest is the region of the north-central United States, including states such as Ohio, Illinois and Iowa.

entries.clue: Muslim hermit is around after a month (8)

indicatorNotes.after: the second piece comes after the month

blocks.note: Mar = March
around = about

annotation.surface: A holy recluse is said to be back in the area after a month away.
annotation.walkthrough: A marabout is a Muslim holy man or hermit in North and West Africa; the word is also the name of a stork.
annotation.definitionFit: A marabout is a Muslim holy man or hermit, especially in North Africa.

entries.clue: Wife no longer referred to as aroused (7)

blocks.note: an ex-wife is a wife no longer
cited = referred to

annotation.surface: A former wife, once called passionate, is no longer described that way.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a marriage gone cold; the definition is at the end, and 'as' only links it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe feelings or passions that have been stirred up.

entries.clue: Senior commander arrests one very unmilitary (5)

indicatorNotes.arrests: the commander holds the others captive inside

blocks.note: CIC = commander-in-chief; this is the outer word
I = one
v = very; with I, placed inside C…IC

annotation.surface: A top general detains a soldier who is not soldierly enough.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all army, which hides that the definition means civilian, the opposite of military.
annotation.definitionFit: Civic means relating to citizens and civil life, not the military.

entries.clue: Convertible option coming from the leader (3,4)

blocks.note: a soft-top car driven with its roof folded away
management jargon for decisions imposed from above

annotation.surface: A choice of open-top car handed down by the boss.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is the car's roof folded back; the second is management jargon for decisions imposed from above.
annotation.definitionFit: Top-down describes both an open convertible and control imposed by the leadership.

entries.clue: Not quite get the better of author, more than satisfied with extravagant fee (15)

annotation.definitionNote: an adjective phrase: overcompensated means paid with an extravagant fee

blocks.clueFragment: Not quite get the better of
blocks.note: OVERCOME without its last letter
to pen is to write, author
sated = filled beyond satisfaction

annotation.surface: A writer nearly beaten, yet more than pleased with a lavish payment.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition hides at the end after a long run of wordplay; 'author' is a verb here, to pen.
annotation.definitionFit: Overcompensated means paid too much, given an extravagant fee.

entries.clue: Overcharge for plant (4)

blocks.note: informal British verb for charging a customer too much
a grass-like plant of marshes, once used for floor mats and candle wicks

annotation.surface: A garden centre charges too much for a plant.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang, to rush a customer is to overcharge them: 'How much did they rush you for that?'
annotation.definitionFit: Rush means both to overcharge and a grass-like marsh plant.

entries.clue: Find one’s about to enter port (8)

indicatorNotes.to enter: the pieces go inside the port

blocks.note: Dover, the English Channel port; this is the outer word
one's = I'S, I being one
c = circa, about; with IS, placed inside D…OVER

annotation.surface: A traveller learns they are about to arrive at the harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is C (circa) and 'to enter' is the instruction. Dover is England's main Channel port.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to come upon something for the first time, as explorers or scientists do.

entries.clue: Tin with dreadful soup — just one star (7)

indicatorNotes.dreadful: the soup is in a dreadful state: its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a tin is a can
SOUP rearranged

annotation.surface: A restaurant review of tinned soup so bad it earns a single star.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a one-star review of canned soup; the star is real, Canopus, the second-brightest in the night sky.
annotation.definitionFit: Canopus is a single star, the brightest in the constellation Carina.

entries.clue: Be in charge and come down to speak (5)

indicatorNotes.to speak: the word is spoken, so only its sound counts

blocks.note: what the weather does when it comes down, said aloud

annotation.surface: A leader is urged to take control and come downstairs to address the people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Come down' is weather: rain falls, and rain is said the same as reign.
annotation.definitionFit: What a monarch does on the throne, extended to anyone who holds sway.

entries.clue: Tutor’s work with small son on sci-fi writer (9)

indicatorNotes.on: the small son comes on after the writer

blocks.note: to go is to work, function
Jules Verne, author of Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
s = small
s = son

annotation.surface: A tutor's own writing, done with a young boy, builds on a science-fiction author.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tutor's work' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Tutor', with 's as 'is'; 'work' is GO, as in 'does it go?'
annotation.definitionFit: A governess is a woman employed to tutor children in a private household.

entries.clue: In dispute, referee’s assistant intended to ignore fine (8)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer is a noun; 'at variance' means in dispute

indicatorNotes.to ignore: the fine is left out of the word

blocks.note: VAR = video assistant referee, in football
one's intended is one's fiancé
f = fine; taken out of FIANCE to leave IANCE

annotation.surface: In a row over a match, the video referee meant to let a penalty go.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Intended' reads as 'meant', but it is a noun: one's intended, a fiancé. VAR is football's video assistant referee.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom 'at variance with' describes parties who disagree, so the noun stands for a state of dispute.

entries.clue: Philosopher isn’t tweeting nonsense (12)

indicatorNotes.nonsense: the letters make nonsense and must be rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A great thinker declines to post rubbish on social media.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: Wittgenstein famously said that whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.
annotation.definitionFit: Ludwig Wittgenstein was an Austrian-British philosopher of language and logic.

entries.clue: Entering hotel, putting specs and card in receptacle (7,2)

indicatorNotes.putting: 'putting' something somewhere is placing it, so the specs and card are placed as the next word directs
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' names where they go: inside the receptacle, whose letters wrap round them

blocks.note: a bin is a receptacle; this is the outer word
two round lenses look like OO
a king is a playing card; with OO, placed inside B…IN

annotation.surface: Checking in at a hotel, a guest drops glasses and a key card into a tray.
annotation.walkthrough: Specs as OO is visual: a pair of spectacles looks like two Os side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: Booking in means registering on arrival at a hotel.

entries.clue: Check competitiveness, not initially courteous behaviour (8)

indicatorNotes.not initially: 'initially' means at the start, so 'not initially' tells you to lose the word's opening letter

blocks.note: ch = check, in chess notation
RIVALRY without its first letter

annotation.surface: Keeping rivalry in check is described as the gentlemanly way to behave.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface frames chivalry as the opposite of rivalry, yet it is built from rivalry with its head cut off.
annotation.definitionFit: Chivalry is courteous, gallant behaviour, especially towards women.

entries.clue: Swimmer’s blue with cold penetrating (4)

indicatorNotes.penetrating: the cold goes into the other word

blocks.note: feeling blue = sad; this is the outer word
c = cold, on taps; placed inside S…AD

annotation.surface: A swimmer turns blue as the cold water gets through to them.
annotation.walkthrough: The swimmer is a fish: the scad, or horse mackerel; 'Swimmer's' means 'Swimmer is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A scad is a fish, also called a horse mackerel.

entries.clue: Applause welcoming a huge success for racing driver (10)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: the applause takes the success into its arms

blocks.note: a cheer is applause; this is the outer word
a riot = a huge success, as in 'the show was a riot'; placed inside CH…EER

annotation.surface: A crowd cheers a Formula One winner after a triumphant race.
annotation.walkthrough: The racing driver is ancient: a charioteer drove in chariot races, not Grand Prix.
annotation.definitionFit: A charioteer drove a chariot, often in races.

entries.clue: Buried away from home, with no confirmation of age (7)

indicatorNotes.away from: the home letters are taken away

blocks.note: buried under, swamped, as in 'buried in work'
at home = in; taken off the front of INUNDATED

annotation.surface: Someone laid to rest abroad, with no proof of how old they were.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a grave, but 'buried' means swamped, as with emails: inundated.
annotation.definitionFit: Something undated bears no date, so its age is unconfirmed.

entries.clue: Supernatural creature I found in gutter, a source of irritation (5,4)

indicatorNotes.found in: the creature and I are found inside the gutter

blocks.note: a ditch is a gutter; this is the outer word
a hob is a goblin or sprite
used as it stands; with HOB, placed inside D…ITCH

annotation.surface: Someone finds a goblin lurking in the drain, which is annoying.
annotation.walkthrough: Dhobi itch is a fungal skin rash of the tropics, named after the dhobi, an Indian washerman.
annotation.definitionFit: Dhobi itch is an itchy fungal skin infection, a literal source of irritation.

entries.clue: Plant college in favoured area (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the college goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: a pet project is a favoured one
uni = university
a = area; PET + A wrap round UNI

annotation.surface: A university is sited in a popular part of town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb, to site a college; it is the definition, a flower.
annotation.definitionFit: The petunia is a garden plant with trumpet-shaped flowers.

entries.clue: Taking principal piece last, fastening up paraphernalia (9)

indicatorNotes.Taking principal piece last: the first letter is moved to the end

blocks.note: strapping up = fastening
the leading letter moves from the front to the back

annotation.surface: Someone packs the most important item last while buckling up a bag of gear.
annotation.walkthrough: The instruction comes first and sounds like packing advice; it tells you to move the leading S of STRAPPING to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Trappings are the accessories and outward trimmings that go with something.

entries.clue: Novel approach, collecting unknown religious literature (9)

indicatorNotes.Novel: a new arrangement of the letters
indicatorNotes.collecting: the fodder takes in the unknown

blocks.note: anagram fodder
y = an unknown in algebra, collected into the fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A fresh take on gathering obscure sacred writings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, fitting 'literature', but it is the anagram indicator; X, Y and Z are the algebraic unknowns.
annotation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are biblical writings not accepted into the canon.

entries.clue: A quiet reputation not at first given to dwarfs’ leader, Bashful (7)

blocks.note: used as it stands
sh! = be quiet
FAME without its first letter
first letter of dwarfs

annotation.surface: Snow White's shy dwarf gets a quiet reputation among the others.
annotation.walkthrough: Bashful is one of Disney's seven dwarfs, so the surface tempts you to look for a dwarf; the name is the definition, meaning embarrassed.
annotation.definitionFit: Ashamed is close to bashful: embarrassed and self-conscious.

entries.clue: Parliament put in a fix by a rigged photo: now there’s a story (3,5,2,4,6)

indicatorNotes.rigged: the photo is faked, its letters rearranged
indicatorNotes.by: beside, next to the other pieces

blocks.note: the House of Commons
A PHOTO rearranged
to corner someone is to put them in a fix

annotation.surface: Parliament is embarrassed by a doctored photograph, and the press has a scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces come in a different order from the clue: the fixed photo sits between the House and the corner. The answer is A. A. Milne's second Winnie-the-Pooh book.
annotation.definitionFit: The House at Pooh Corner is A. A. Milne's 1928 collection of Winnie-the-Pooh stories.

entries.clue: Counter Reformation composer shortly to meet his monarch (7)

indicatorNotes.shortly: cut short: the last letter goes

blocks.note: Thomas TALLIS, Tudor composer, without his last letter
ER = Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth I, whom Tallis served

annotation.surface: A composer of the Counter-Reformation is briefly presented to his sovereign.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Counter Reformation' is a famous phrase, but the definition is 'Counter' alone: one who tallies. Tallis composed through the English Reformation.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps a tally, adding up a score or stock, is a counter in the agent-noun sense.

entries.clue: Second demonstrator’s moral lesson (7)

blocks.note: one who proves, demonstrates
B is second, after A

annotation.surface: A second teacher is giving a lesson in ethics.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces go in the other order from the clue; 'demonstrator' looks like a protester but is one who demonstrates, a prover.
annotation.definitionFit: A proverb is a short saying carrying a moral lesson.

entries.clue: Law on drink performs badly (4,2)

blocks.note: an act of parliament is a law
to sup is to drink

annotation.surface: Legislation on alcohol is working poorly.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a licensing law failing; 'acts up' is a machine or a child misbehaving.
annotation.definitionFit: Something that acts up malfunctions or behaves badly.

entries.clue: Settle to repair what’s unravelling? (6)

blocks.note: to settle a bill or pay costs
an invented word: the prefix that undoes, as in de-ice, plus the word for unravelling

annotation.surface: Someone thinks about how to mend a fraying garment.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer as DE + FRAY, like de-ice or de-frost; the question mark flags the invented word.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal word used almost only of expenses: paying a bill is settling it.

entries.clue: Look into swimming costume, a bit short for very large figures (7)

indicatorNotes.into: the look goes into the costume
indicatorNotes.a bit short: the costume loses its last letter

blocks.note: COSSIE, British and Australian slang for a swimsuit, without its last letter; the outer word
lo! = look; placed inside CO…SSI

annotation.surface: Peeking at a skimpy swimsuit worn by some large people.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is saucy, which hides the definition: colossi are giant statues, like the Colossus of Rhodes. A cossie is slang for a swimming costume.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Figures' means statues: the Colossus of Rhodes was a giant bronze statue, and its Latin plural names any such giants.

entries.clue: Sort of love some tea with meals provided (8)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer is the word that goes with 'love' in 'cupboard love'

blocks.note: a cup of tea
board = meals provided, as in bed and board

annotation.surface: Affection for whoever serves the tea and dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: Cupboard love is affection shown for what you can get, like a cat loving whoever feeds it, which is exactly the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Cupboard love is affection shown only in hope of reward, such as food.

entries.clue: Blokes’ fortune in type of gas (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the fortune goes inside the gas

blocks.note: CS gas, a tear gas; this is the outer word
hap = luck, fortune; placed inside C…S

annotation.surface: Some men's wealth is tied up in industrial gas.
annotation.walkthrough: CS gas is the tear gas used in riot control; 'hap' is an old word for chance, as in hapless.
annotation.definitionFit: Chaps and blokes are both British words for men.

entries.clue: Following collapse close crew’s quarters (6)

indicatorNotes.collapse: the word falls apart and its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: f = following, as in p. 5f
CLOSE rearranged

annotation.surface: After a building falls down, the sailors' living area is shut.
annotation.walkthrough: The fo'c'sle, short for forecastle, is the front of a ship where the crew traditionally lived.
annotation.definitionFit: The fo'c'sle is the forward part of a ship, where the crew's quarters were.

entries.clue: Sparingly eat a measure of grain (4)

blocks.note: to nibble at food like a bird
an old dry measure, a quarter of a bushel

annotation.surface: Advice to eat just a little grain.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a bird pecking at grain; both halves are definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: To peck is to eat in small bites, and a peck is a dry measure of grain.

entries.clue: Loaded information at end of magazine column (5)

blocks.note: spin = information slanted to favour one side
last letter of magazine

annotation.surface: A biased news item runs at the back of a magazine column.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Column' looks like a newspaper column; here it is the spinal column.
annotation.definitionFit: An anatomical sense of 'column': the vertebral column, stacked bones running down the back.

entries.clue: Novice to shower wearing shirt (7)

indicatorNotes.wearing: the shower is worn inside the shirt

blocks.note: a tee shirt; this is the outer word
a shower of rain; placed inside T…EE

annotation.surface: A beginner is told to shower with their shirt still on.
annotation.walkthrough: The shower is weather, not a bathroom, and the shirt wears it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name a beginner still learning a job.

entries.clue: Piano, late alternative for leader of singing (9)

blocks.note: p = piano, soft, in music
the late news is the recent news
or introduces an alternative

annotation.surface: A choir hears that the piano is late and a stand-in must lead them.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all music, so 'Piano' reads as the instrument; it is the dynamic marking p.
annotation.definitionFit: A precentor leads the singing in a church or synagogue.

entries.clue: Digression as man interrupts two relatives (11)

indicatorNotes.interrupts: the man breaks into the relatives

blocks.note: the first relative, with SIS the outer pair
he = a man; placed between the two relatives
sis = sister, the second relative

annotation.surface: A family conversation goes off-topic when a man cuts in.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface fits: a parenthesis is itself an interruption, the man breaking in just as a bracketed aside does.
annotation.definitionFit: A parenthesis is an aside or digression inserted into a passage.

entries.clue: Refuse to deal with brawl: I had come in time for a bargain (5,6)

blocks.note: to black goods is to boycott them, as a union might
a fray is a fight; the outer word
I'd = I had; placed inside FR…AY

annotation.surface: A shop worker refuses to deal with a fight that broke out in the sales rush.
annotation.walkthrough: To black something is British trade-union language for refusing to handle it; Black Friday is the day of sales after US Thanksgiving.
annotation.definitionFit: Black Friday is the post-Thanksgiving shopping day famous for bargains.
